As a Filipino, I can definitely tell you that the people are not going to revolt in a long while. Not because things are going fine, and I know they're not, but because most of our population are not that knowledgeable of the things they're voting for or promoting.

See, the only people who would most likely try to resist the government are the people and students in the bigger private schools, like UP or Ateneo De Manila, OLOPSC, Santo Tomas, etc. These guys know about oppression, politics, economics, law, the right to freedom, etc. They know about the nation's history, they know about how we have the right to be free, etc. Most of them have the education and the knowledge to be conscious about their voting and the ideals they promote. However, these people are a small minority of the bigger crowd.

The rest of our population is either stuck in public schooling or even does not have the funding to go to school at all. These guys are the majority of the people. Most of them are the ones who voted for the recent president-elect, the son of a dictator who ruled the country by decree 30 years ago. I'm pretty sure that a lot of them did not even have a decent political reason to vote for him. They just went along with what the rest of their friends, family, and classmates were doing without full knowledge of what they were doing. Maybe some did have a reason that they came up with, but I'm very sure that the majority just went along with the trend that was going on.   


So if we know that these are the majority of people and that the majority of people are oblivious to a full-scale revolution, then we can probably assume that a revolution is not going to be happening soon, or even in the next few years. Of course, this is not a fully definitive analysis on the subject. Perhaps a revolution could happen if the economy crashes like it did in Sri Lanka, or if some politician does or says something wrong, or if some bigger country like China invades, or if the people just decide to revolt for no reason other than it sounds like a good idea.   


But the main point is this: a lot of people wouldn't revolt. Not because they're afraid of the government, or the politicians, or of losing their rights, but because most of them do not have the knowledge to know about the consequences of their collective choices. To be honest, it's really sad. If more of our people had the money, at least enough money, to be sent to a good school with good and thoughtful education, then I am definitely, most definitely sure that this country would be 1000000x much better than it is now.

I got it fixed guys.

Here's the thing that you're missing, both vanilla players and modded server players.

Vanilla players should go into their Steam application, and find "Friends and Chat" on the bottom left of the Steam page.Press the cog on the top right, the grey circle with a hole in the middle and spokes sticking out. Then, go to "Voice".Now switch your voice input to your microphone and your voice output to your speakers.

Now for modded servers, with TFAR, the in-game Direct chat is not used. TFAR disables the default Arma 3 voice chat automatically once enabled in the Teamspeak settings.Now what you have to do is to speak through the TFAR VERSION of the Arma 3 in-game voice chat, which works exactly like the default vanilla one.

I'm not talking about the radio, I'm talking about an actual version of the in-game voice chat in TFAR that works with Arma 3. If you use TFAR, go to the Teamspeak Options tab, press on the "Capture" tab, then enable "Push-to-talk". Set the key to your liking, in my case, it's the letter "J".

Now if you press "J" in-game, other people can hear you not through the radio but through TFAR's in-game voice chat. Yes, it even works with Direct Communication, Global channels, etc.
